To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a hypertension susceptibility locus in Scandinavians at 14q21.1.
we have found a hypertension susceptibility locus at chromosome 14q22.3-24.2 and that we have replicated a hypertension susceptibility locus in the vicinity of D14S1027 at 14q22.
a genome wide scan for primary hypertension in Scandinavia identified two promising loci, one on chromosome 14 and one on chromosome 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for hypertension susceptibility genes in Scandinavians, which is a genetically homogenous population.
the genetic basis for primary hypertension and the identification of genes involved in its pathophysiology.
identifying genetic loci that contribute to early onset primary hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present genome scan does not exclude any of the loci found in the 10 c M genome wide scan.
we have identified a locus on chromosome 1 at 80 cM (P =0.0002).
we have identified two promising regions on chromosomes 2 and 14, which are worthy of further study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our data support the presence of a major locus for early onset primary arterial hypertension, which has been previously suggested by other studies.
we found a hypertension susceptibility locus with a genome wide level of significance, which is a novel finding.

our data support the existence of a hypertension susceptibility locus in the vicinity of the chromosome 2q33-35 region, and that the chromosome 14p12-13 region is a possible candidate for a susceptibility gene for early onset hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a genome scan with a density of 10 cM is sufficient to detect hypertension susceptibility loci.
the genetic architecture of early-onset hypertension differs from that of late-onset hypertension.
a genome wide scan for primary hypertension is possible and that it can be used as an effective tool in the identification of susceptibility genes for this disease.
